{{nihongo|'''Wanikawa Shrine'''|鰐河神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sanuki Province]].

'''Wanikawa Shrine''' (わにかわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Miki, Kagawa|arz|بلده ميكى|ca|Miki (Kagawa)|ceb|Miki Chō|es|Miki (Kagawa)|fa|میکی، کاگاوا|fr|Miki (Kagawa)|id|Miki, Kagawa|it|Miki (Kagawa)|ja|三木町|ko|미키정|ms|Miki, Kagawa|pl|Miki (Kagawa)|ro|Miki, Kagawa|ru|Мики (посёлок)|sv|Miki, Kagawa|tl|Miki, Kagawa|tr|Miki, Kagawa|uk|Мікі (Каґава)|ur|میکی، کاگاوا|zh|三木町|qid=Q1205980}}, {{ill|Kita District, Kagawa|ca|Districte de Kita (Kagawa)|ceb|Kita-gun (distrito sa Hapon, Kagawa-ken)|es|Distrito de Kita (Kagawa)|fr|District de Kita (Kagawa)|id|Distrik Kita, Kagawa|it|Distretto di Kita (Kagawa)|ja|木田郡|ko|기타군 (가가와현)|pl|Powiat Kita (Kagawa)|pt|Distrito de Kita|uk|Повіт Кіта (Каґава)|zh|木田郡|qid=Q1155929}}, {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|Q161454|qid=Q161454}}. It is one of the candidate shrines for Wanigawa Shrine, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} of Takaoka-go, {{ill|Miki district|Q10866143|qid=Q10866143}}, {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}}. It is one of the “Sanuki Fifteen Shrines.”

There is a theory that {{ill|Hakusan Shrine (Q11579589)|Q11579589|qid=Q11579589|lt=Hakusan Shrine}}, also a candidate shrine for Wanigawa Shrine, is an outside branch shrine of Wanikawa Shrine.

=== Outline ===
The founding period is unknown. According to shrine tradition, {{ill|Toyotama-hime|de|Toyotama-hime|es|Toyotama-hime|fa|تویوتاما-هیمه|fi|Otohime|fr|Otohime|id|Toyotama-hime|ja|トヨタマヒメ|ko|도요타마히메|mni|ꯇꯣꯌꯣꯇꯃ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Toyotama-hime|ru|Тоётама-химэ|simple|Toyotama-hime|sv|Otohime|uk|Тойотама-хіме|vi|Toyotama-hime|zh|豐玉毘賣命|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime-no-Mikoto}} rode a {{ill|Cheloniidae|ar|لجئيات|arz|سلاحف بحريه|ban|Cheloniidae|be|Марскія чарапахі|bg|Морски костенурки|bjn|Biyuku|br|Cheloniidae|ca|Quelònids|ceb|Cheloniidae|cs|Karetovití|de|Meeresschildkröten|ee|Ƒumeklo|es|Cheloniidae|eu|Cheloniidae|fa|لاک‌پشتان دریایی|fi|Merikilpikonnat|fr|Cheloniidae|gl|Quelónidos|he|צבים ימיים|hu|Tengeriteknős-félék|is|Sæskjaldbökur|it|Cheloniidae|ja|ウミガメ科|kk|Теңіз тасбақалары|ko|바다거북과|ky|Деңиз таш бакасы|lt|Jūriniai vėžliai|mg|Tano|ms|Cheloniidae|nl|Zeeschildpadden|no|Cheloniidae|pl|Żółwie morskie|pnb|سمندری کھچوپڑے|pt|Queloniídeos|ro|Cheloniidae|ru|Морские черепахи|sco|Cheloniidae|sv|Havssköldpaddor|th|วงศ์เต่าทะเล|tr|Cheloniidae|uk|Морські черепахи (родина)|uz|Dengiz toshbaqalari|vi|Họ Vích|war|Cheloniidae|wuu|海龟科|zh|海龜科|zh_min_nan|Hái-ku|qid=Q30143|lt=turtle}} ashore at Kata-moto in {{ill|Yamada district|ja|山田郡 (香川県)|zh|山田郡 (香川縣)|qid=Q11046466|lt=Yamada District}}, {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}} (near {{ill|Yashima|Q11465681|qid=Q11465681}}), gave birth to {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|qid=Q1373935|lt=Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto}} there, then rode a {{ill|wani|ja|鰐|qid=Q11674313}} upstream and landed here.

There is also a tradition that {{ill|Gyōki|ar|جيوكي|de|Gyōki|es|Gyōki|fr|Gyōki|ja|行基|ko|교기 (승려)|pl|Gyōki|ru|Гёки|zh|行基|qid=Q1136664}} founded it here.

In {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} 7 ({{ill|907|ab|907|af|907|am|907 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|907|ar|907|ary|907|arz|907|ast|907|avk|907|az|907|azb|۹۰۷ (میلادی)|bcl|907|be|907|be_x_old|907|bg|907|bn|৯০৭|bpy|মারি ৯০৭|br|907|bs|907.|ca|907|cdo|907 nièng|ceb|907|ckb|٩٠٧|crh|907|cs|907|csb|907|cv|907|cy|907|da|907|de|907|el|907|eml|907|eo|907|es|907|et|907|eu|907|fa|۹۰۷ (میلادی)|fi|907|fo|907|fr|907|fy|907|ga|907|gan|907年|gd|907|gl|907|he|907|hi|907|hr|907.|ht|907 (almanak jilyen)|hu|907|hy|907|id|907|ilo|907|io|907|is|907|it|907|ja|907年|jv|907|ka|907|kaa|907|kk|907 жыл|ko|907년|la|907|lb|907|lij|907|lmo|907|lt|907 m.|lv|907. gads|map_bms|907|mdf|907|mg|907|mhr|907|mi|907|mk|907|mr|इ.स. ९०७|mrj|907 и|ms|907|mzn|۹۰۷|nah|907|nap|907|nds|907|new|सन् ९०७|nl|907|nn|907|no|907|nrm|907|nso|907|oc|907|or|୯୦୭|os|907-æм аз|pl|907|pnb|907|pt|907|qu|907|ro|907|ru|907 год|rue|907|sa|९०७|sah|907|scn|907|sd|907ع|se|907|sh|907.|shn|907|si|907|sk|907|sl|907|smn|907|sq|907|sr|907|su|907|sv|907|sw|907|tg|Соли 907|th|พ.ศ. 1450|tk|907|tl|907|tly|907|tr|907|tt|907 ел|uk|907|ur|907ء|uz|907|vec|907|vi|907|war|907|wuu|907年|xmf|907|zh|907年|zh_min_nan|907 nî|zh_yue|907年|qid=Q24163}}), the {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}} was enshrined as an associated deity, and it was also called Takaoka Hachiman. Through {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}, Ōjin-ji was also founded as its {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}}.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 1 ({{ill|1868|ab|1868|af|1868|als|1868|am|1868 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1868|ar|1868|ary|1868|arz|1868|ast|1868|avk|1868|az|1868|azb|۱۸۶۸ (میلادی)|ba|1868 йыл|ban|1868|bar|1868|bcl|1868|be|1868|be_x_old|1868|bg|1868|bn|১৮৬৮|bpy|মারি ১৮৬৮|br|1868|bs|1868.|ca|1868|cdo|1868 nièng|ce|1868 шо|ceb|1868|ckb|١٨٦٨|crh|1868|cs|1868|csb|1868|cv|1868|cy|1868|da|1868|de|1868|diq|1868|el|1868|eml|1868|eo|1868|es|1868|et|1868|eu|1868|fa|۱۸۶۸ (میلادی)|fi|1868|fiu_vro|1868|fo|1868|fr|1868|frp|1868|frr|1868|fur|1868|fy|1868|ga|1868|gan|1868年|gcr|1868|gd|1868|gl|1868|gv|1868|hak|1868-ngièn|he|1868|hi|१८६८|hif|1868|hr|1868.|hsb|1868|ht|1868 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1868|hy|1868|hyw|1868 թուական|ia|1868|id|1868|ilo|1868|io|1868|is|1868|it|1868|ja|1868年|jv|1868|ka|1868|kaa|1868|kk|1868 жыл|kn|೧೮೬೮|ko|1868년|krc|1868 джыл|ku|1868|kv|1868-ӧд во|la|1868|lb|1868|lez|1868 йис|li|1868|lij|1868|lmo|1868|lt|1868 m.|lv|1868. gads|mai|१८६८|map_bms|1868|mdf|1868|mg|1868|mhr|1868|mi|1868|min|1868|mk|1868|ml|1868|mr|इ.स. १८६८|mrj|1868 и|ms|1868|my|၁၈၆၈|myv|1868 ие|mzn|۱۸۶۸|nah|1868|nap|1868|nds|1868|new|ई सं १८६८|nl|1868|nn|1868|no|1868|nrm|1868|nso|1868|oc|1868|olo|1868|or|୧୮୬୮|os|1868-æм аз|pa|1868|pap|1868|pl|1868|pnb|1868|pt|1868|qu|1868|ro|1868|roa_rup|1868|ru|1868 год|rue|1868|sa|१८६८|sah|1868|scn|1868|sco|1868|sd|1868ع|se|1868|sh|1868.|shn|1868|si|1868|simple|1868|sk|1868|sl|1868|smn|1868|sq|1868|sr|1868|stq|1868|su|1868|sv|1868|sw|1868|szl|1868|ta|1868|te|1868|tg|Соли 1868|th|พ.ศ. 2411|tk|1868|tl|1868|tly|1868|tr|1868|tt|1868 ел|udm|1868 ар|uk|1868|ur|1868ء|uz|1868|vec|1868|vi|1868|vls|1868|vo|1868|wa|1868|war|1868|wuu|1868年|xmf|1868|yi|1868|za|1868 nienz|zea|1868|zh|1868年|zh_classical|一八六八年|zh_min_nan|1868 nî|zh_yue|1868年|qid=Q7717}}), Ōjin-ji was abolished in the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}. In Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it was renamed Wanikawa Shrine and became {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Other ===
* The lion head for Wanikawa Shrine’s {{ill|Lion dance|arz|رقصة الاسد|as|সিংহ নৃত্য|ast|Danza del lleón|ban|Barongsai|be|Танец ільва|bew|Barongsay|bjn|Barungsai|cdo|Páh-săi|ckb|سەمای شێر|cs|Lví tanec|de|Löwentanz|es|Danza del león|fa|رقص شیر|fr|Danse du lion|gor|Barongsai|he|ריקוד האריה|hu|Oroszlántánc|hy|Առյուծի պար|id|Barongsai|it|Danza del leone|ja|獅子舞|jv|Barongsai|ko|사자춤|min|Tari Barongsai|ms|Tarian singa|nl|Leeuwendans|pl|Taniec lwów|pt|Dança do leão|ru|Танец льва|sat|ᱠᱩᱞ ᱮᱱᱮᱡ|su|Barongsai|sv|Sing Si|ta|சீன சிங்க நடனம்|th|การเชิดสิงโต|tl|Sayaw ng leon|tr|Aslan dansı|uk|Танець лева|vi|Múa lân - sư - rồng|za|Foux Saeceij|zh|舞獅|zh_min_nan|Lāng-sai|zh_yue|舞獅|qid=Q713866}} is 63 cm high, 90 cm wide, and 100 cm long; with the dance cloth, total length is about 13 m. This giant lion dance is moved by about 50 people and is a designated cultural property of Miki Town.
* The seated dry-lacquer {{ill|Āryāvalokiteśvara|Q124684411|qid=Q124684411}} statue at Gankō-ji in {{ill|Sanuki, Kagawa|ar|سانوكي (كاغاوا)|azb|سان‌اوکی، کاقاوا|ca|Sanuki|ce|Сануки|ceb|Sanuki-shi|cs|Sanuki (Kagawa)|de|Sanuki (Kagawa)|es|Sanuki (Kagawa)|fa|سان‌اوکی، کاگاوا|fi|Sanuki|fr|Sanuki|gl|Sanuki|hak|Sanuki-sṳ|he|סנוקי|hy|Սանուկի|id|Sanuki, Kagawa|it|Sanuki|ja|さぬき市|ko|사누키시|mzn|سان‌اوکی، کاگاوا|nl|Sanuki (Kagawa)|pl|Sanuki (miasto)|pt|Sanuki (Kagawa)|ro|Sanuki|ru|Сануки|sv|Sanuki|tg|Сануки|tl|Sanuki, Kagawa|tr|Sanuki|tt|Сануки|uk|Санукі (Каґава)|ur|سانوکی، کاگاوا|uz|Sanuki|vi|Sanuki, Kagawa|war|Sanuki, Kagawa|zh|讚岐市|zh_classical|讚岐市|zh_min_nan|Sanuki-chhī|zh_yue|讚岐|qid=Q857202}} is said in tradition to have been the principal image of Ōjin-ji, the bettō temple of Wanikawa Shrine.
* The river that Toyotama-hime rode upstream on a wani later became Wani River, said to be today’s {{ill|Shinkawa River|Q11502062|qid=Q11502062|lt=Shinkawa}}. According to nearby {{ill|Wanikawa Shrine (Q11417869)|Q11417869|qid=Q11417869}} (another candidate shrine), Wani River refers to {{ill|Kabe River|Q11675608|qid=Q11675608}}.

=== Access ===
* 20 minutes on foot from {{ill|Shirayama Station|Q11579619|qid=Q11579619|lt=Hakusan Station}} on the {{ill|Kotoden Nagao Line|Q5364831|qid=Q5364831}} of {{ill|Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railroad|Q566998|qid=Q566998}}.
